records.signal: For the large FP16 input, adjacent double-block prefetch reduced Vector idle and MTE3 waits, but device-task latency rose from 39.26 to 49.64 us and the full score fell from 0.915250 to 0.750783 times CANN.
records.mechanism: Waiting may shift to MTE2 or Vector; input transfer granularity also fell from about 16.48 KB to 5.41 KB. Source prefetch does not prove compiled overlap, and reduced idle/wait in one component cannot replace whole-call validation.
records.action: Compare productive/wait-only/idle intervals for the same source, case, and core window; correlate actual IR loop-carried values and transfer organization, then return full performance failures to the generator. A later loop-carried revision recovered to 0.833512 times CANN but remained below the starter; retain the existing delivery.
constraints: Observations apply to log10_, FP16, 4096x4096, and this compiler environment, not all elementwise operators.
Loop-carried tensors in IR establish value dependencies, not physical double buffering or the critical path.
Simulator and hardware activate different core counts. Use the simulator for within-model region comparisons and full KGS device results for gains.

records.signal: The fixed FlagGems starter falls back to PyTorch on non-CUDA devices and uses contiguous/copy_ for strided paths; the historical strict-Triton version passed all 36 formal cases and 66 supplementary cases per reference.
records.mechanism: log10 uses natural logarithm times a base-conversion constant. Explicit FP32 promotion and input-dtype math produce different actual IR and must be compared under fixed precision requirements. Inspect host launch for small inputs, concurrent programs/UB footprint/contiguous transfers for large inputs, and real-stride in-place access for strided inputs.
records.action: The generator must remove device-side PyTorch fallbacks and implement contiguous, uniform-stride, and general multidimensional paths. Check continuous-path payloads and loop geometry first: historical methods use large direct tiles for medium inputs and adjacent paired streaming on a bounded grid for the largest input, rather than universally limiting work to 4096 elements and 40 programs. Try larger contiguous payloads fitting UB; verify compile-time loop bounds/steps. Exactly divisible paired payloads may remove dynamic masks. Reuse launcher caching while validating current stream and per-call pointer alignment.
constraints: All candidate computation, copies, and layout handling use strict Triton; contiguous, copy_, or CANN cannot implement strided paths.
Preserve negative inputs, signed zero, NaN, Inf, and FP16/BF16/FP32 semantics; ordinary positive-input checks cannot replace special-value validation.

Validated in development: with unchanged layout, tiles, and launch path, removing only explicit FP32 casts from the math helper kept log and base-conversion multiplication in input dtype and improved the formal score from 0.761426 to 0.851055 times CANN. TTIR/bcmlir changed FP16/BF16 extf->FP32 log/mul->truncf into input-dtype log/mul; FP32 was unchanged. All 36 formal, 66 supplementary per reference, and 15 tiny-value/nondivisible-tail checks passed. This is a mechanism to test under the fixed contract, not relaxed tolerances or a universal reduced-precision rule. Regeneration must recheck negatives, signed zero, NaN, Inf, tiny positives, values near one, and all layouts.

The reduced-precision observation binds source 8600ce07031842c6bed467ea5ebe1f0a66d265e864b171e4176c1f0b6b318324 and comparison 69699663ecc7. Originals are formal-8600ce070318, edge-checks-8600ce070318.json, and compiler-comparison-8600ce070318.json under log10-method-transfer-20261110-development-v2. Gains come from formal timing; IR type changes alone do not establish an arithmetic-only bottleneck or exclude host/movement effects.

Nested JIT dependency checks compare captured module globals. Floating-point module-level NaN may falsely trigger conflicts because NaN differs from itself. For explicit Global variable...nan...conflicting value nan errors, the generator must change device-side special-constant construction without deleting NaN semantics or bypassing checks. This compile error says nothing about approximation accuracy or performance.

The compiler forbids direct JIT reads of ordinary module scalars. Use actual tl.constexpr objects or local literals as required by errors; a constexpr type annotation alone is insufficient. Do not bypass this with TRITON_ALLOW_NON_CONSTEXPR_GLOBALS. Verify all constants captured by new device functions rather than patching omissions one by one.
Pointer alignment belongs to the current input, not just its shape. Identical-shape offsets 0/1/3/0 must pass without corrupting adjacent storage.
Use real shape/stride for strided layouts. Merge contiguous dimensions to reduce dynamic elementwise division, but do not assume every view has a uniform stride.

Dimension merging must retain the innermost stride. Shape [2,3], stride [3,1] becomes shape [6], stride [1]; retaining the outer stride causes out-of-bounds access. Prefer flat addressing for contiguous inputs instead of scattered access caused by incorrect merged metadata.

UB overflow may result from scattered buffers inflated by wrong strides. Verify address mappings before shrinking tiles blindly; perform read-only execution-path/boundary review for the current SHA before device preflight.
Bounded-grid loops and double-block prefetch require validation on current source and do not inherit historical gains. Oversized tiles may fail UB allocation at compile time.

TTIR load/compute/store order does not prove absent hardware overlap, and two source loads do not guarantee concurrent in-flight work. If double-block edits do not improve full performance, do not claim memory latency is solved; inspect masks, buffer footprint, and host argument parsing while retaining the prior plan.

If actual IR still creates per-element dynamic masks for the second load/store in a full-block branch, inspect pairing and loop steps. Cross-grid pairing can leave the second block invalid even when total size divides one tile. Adjacent pairs with paired loop steps may remove masks under divisibility, but recheck tails, disjoint program coverage, UB, and full performance rather than merely deleting masks.

When large-input timings are similar across dtypes, test per-program iteration count as a hypothesis. For 16777216 elements, 40 programs, and 4096 elements per iteration, about 102-103 iterations are needed. Larger contiguous payloads may reduce loop/task overhead. Test 8192 or more within UB and verify compile-time bounds/steps. Coverage arithmetic does not prove a Scalar bottleneck; gains require full performance validation.

Read-only historical-source observation: medium contiguous inputs used at most 32768 elements per total tile; the largest input used 40 programs and two adjacent 8192-element payloads, with constexpr loop length/subtile size. This is a fact about bound historical source, not current-candidate gains or a complete transferable implementation. The generator receives geometry/mechanism information only and must implement/revalidate tails, UB, dtypes, and layouts. Failure of current 4096-element dynamic loops does not refute larger contiguous payloads.

Development failure: ninth-order Taylor replacement of tl.log in candidate 81e71eae required 4194560 bits of UB versus 1572864 available during layout-path compilation; it never reached formal performance evaluation. Native tl.log had passed fully but did not yet restore historical payload geometry. Revert unvalidated math approximations, restore validated math, then implement scale-specific paths and larger contiguous payloads. Do not shrink every path and increase iterations merely to fit complex unvalidated approximations. This recommendation follows compile failure and missing method components, not proof of a unique transcendental or memory bottleneck.

Unmasked paired main-loop counts must use genuinely full blocks. Ceiling block counts may include incomplete tails: N=65535, subtile=8192, grid=4 gives 8 total blocks, but block 8 lacks one element and cannot be included in an unmasked 8-block round. Full main loops and masked tails must cover all elements without overlap. Repair statically proven out-of-bounds access before running on hardware.
Formal feedback covers small inputs and the largest input per dtype; device profiling cannot replace full KGS call scores.
records.attribution: Codex extracted methods from historical diagnostics, source, and full results; only CC/DeepSeek generates and edits subsequent candidates.

records.signal: Several small-input full calls take about 80-85 us versus about 13 us for CANN; large and small inputs have different performance losses.
records.mechanism: Historical implementations cached compiled launchers, function handles, packed metadata, and metadata, launching Triton artifacts with current pointers/streams. Regenerated versions used ordinary JIT dispatch without this path. Comparing the two full implementations is not a single-variable causal experiment.
records.action: Cover small and largest inputs by geometric-mean loss. Verify current launcher ABI/constexpr slots and cache compiled handles/host metadata. When JIT hits still leave a small-input plateau, use current host stacks to reduce Python layers and repeated metadata queries. A proven contiguous flat path may cache dtype, numel, actual alignment class, and device without rebuilding full shapes/strides every call; strided paths retain full layout identity. Query raw stream/addresses dynamically under the local backend contract and retain ordinary Triton fallback when conditions fail.
constraints: Read the current stream and verify device, dtype, numel, stride, and pointer alignment on each call; never cache tensor results or stale streams.
Cold calls execute in-place computation exactly once; handle unaligned inputs, strided layouts, tails, and profiling modes correctly.
Launcher ABI follows current compiled artifacts; Python/C++ host bridges cannot perform target device computation.
Historical 1.039292 times CANN versus ordinary-dispatch 0.210037 describes two implementations; new candidates need full evaluation and inherit no speedup.
Report ordinary call time, device-event span, and device-task duration separately; event span is not automatically device-only execution time.
Query function objects may be cached, but dynamic current-device, stream, and pointer values cannot.

Fast-path tables accept only ordinary compiled artifacts after excluding compile-only, debug, and capture-specific modes. Do not mix artifacts across modes. Check at the actual lifecycle stage: NPULauncher fixes compile_only, tensor registration, and metadata at construction, while active HookChain callbacks vary at runtime.
Do not share mutable launch-argument arrays or fall back by resubmitting in-place computation after a launch exception.
NoWait applicability follows the current Triton backend queue contract and stream tests, not its interface name.
Compiled-artifact cache keys include device identity. Query current stream/pointers dynamically; never reuse the first device handle unconditionally on another device.

Cold calls may start before a cache container exists, so old-dictionary key differences alone cannot identify new artifacts. Register the actually used object from current JIT return values/artifact interfaces and verify real cache hits in diagnostics.
Locate debug/capture hooks from current API facts. Report import failures causing permanent ordinary dispatch; source-level cache structures do not prove a working fast path.

Direct compiled-launcher calls must retain every argument slot defined by the current generator. constexpr values may retain PyObject placeholders in the Python ABI even when omitted from device arguments. Do not build ABI from dynamic arguments alone or mistake permanent TypeError fallback for fast-path success.

A debug hook may be an always-present HookChain container. A non-None object does not mean active callbacks; use current empty-chain semantics and respect real callbacks. Verify fast paths using cold/warm JIT counts and cache size, not cache existence alone.

If JIT counts are zero but full calls remain slow, sample warm-call host stacks for layout merging, specialization strings, backend strategy registries, and Python launch wrappers. cProfile cumulative time includes callees and sampling overhead; it is not additive or formal performance. Confirm gains with fixed KGS evaluation.

Common contiguous paths may check contiguity first and then use immutable layout/grid/full-ABI metadata caches, avoiding repeated dimension merging/string construction. Keys cover dtype, device, numel, actual alignment, and specialization class. Do not cache tensors, pointers, or dynamic streams; retain correct generic paths for strided/unaligned inputs.

Verify current NPULauncher.__call__ and native launch entry. Lightweight launch is allowed only for ordinary artifacts excluding compile-only, tensor registration, hidden debug arguments, and active hooks. Cache query functions/immutable metadata, but read current device/pointers/raw stream dynamically. Removing strategy-dispatch layers must preserve stream correctness.

If a cold in-place call registers artifacts via ordinary JIT, it already executed computation and must not execute the plan again. Validate exactly-once computation for cold and warm paths. Active-hook branches must actually enter ordinary JIT rather than a nominal slow function still calling the native entry directly.

Cached plans follow current compile/debug lifecycles: exclude nonordinary launchers at construction and respect active callbacks at runtime. Register new-mode artifacts separately; preserve hidden debug arguments. Do not assume ordinary JIT rereads environment variables on existing instances each call. torch_npu may wrap environ.get, making repeated queries host overhead. Never resubmit an entire multi-operation in-place plan after partial launch.

If native launch stays slow, inspect current getPointer: Tensor inputs call data_ptr then aclrtPointerGetAttributes each time, while integer addresses parse directly. A validated ordinary warm path may use dynamically queried integer addresses after checking device, dtype, layout, actual alignment, and specialization; compilation/ordinary JIT retain Tensors for proper specialization. Reject blind integer-pointer use for CPU/mismatched devices, never cache addresses, and respect debug/capture paths. This optimizes host parsing for the same Triton artifact; full evaluation determines gains.

Counterexample from log10_ source 69699663: across 50 small-input calls, _plan_key accumulated 0.000204970 seconds, about 4.10 sampled cumulative us per call; run and _run_one self time totaled about 9.71 us per call. Do not misread this as about 1 us total Python time or formal performance. This source reads full shape/stride every call; a lightweight N key for contiguous flat paths remains independently testable. Later math-dtype-only source 8600ce070318 exceeded 0.8 under the same formal contract. Under that target-only experiment, retain/freeze accepted bytes instead of applying every possible method.

findings: After large-input tiling changes, latencies were about 45.5/83.2/82.5 us; small-input calls recovered from ordinary-dispatch about 80 us to about 13-15 us.
Investigate high-level stream construction, synchronizing queries, and repeated host checks separately; empty-queue query microbenchmarks do not represent alternating-launch costs.

records.signal: Ordinary values are correct but zero signs differ
records.mechanism: Historical Triton negation lowered to 0-x and could lose required negative-zero semantics
records.action: Check actual TTIR; test sign-bit flipping and revalidate zeros, NaN/Inf, all dtypes, and layouts
constraints: Ordinary-value tests do not establish special-value correctness
Larger tiles require a new UB check

records.signal: Total read/write volume matches, but Vector/movement instruction counts and candidate time are higher
records.mechanism: Stable formulas, type widening, and buffer lifetimes jointly affect performance
records.action: Inspect near-zero formulas, actual IR, tiles, and blocks per iteration by dtype; validate full calls
constraints: Fewer IR conversions do not guarantee lower latency
Passing FP16 inputs does not replace BF16 range checks
Preserve near-zero error, negative zero, and first-call semantics

records.signal: GM/L1 totals are nearly unchanged while UB traffic and MTE instructions differ
records.mechanism: Reuse direction across adjacent output blocks changes internal organization; gains need not come from reduced HBM traffic
records.action: Compare shared A/B, K tiling, and interleaving using actual bcmlir, transfer granularity, and full evaluation
constraints: Static copy counts are not dynamic transfer counts
Hotspot source mapping does not assign exclusive elapsed time to a Python expression

records.signal: Conflict-free writes remain slow, with per-element loops appearing after TTIR lowering
records.mechanism: A specific FP16 compilation lowered vector atomic writes into per-lane stores
records.action: Inspect current candidate IR and indexing, then test grouping or output-block reductions
constraints: Do not generalize to all dtypes/shapes
Full-call timing includes preprocessing, scratch work, and conversions
Validate atomic-accumulation accuracy independently

records.signal: Flat indexing produces scattered read/write loops and many output instructions
records.mechanism: Explicit sequence-by-head_dim tiling improves compiled transfer organization
records.action: Compare actual ttadapter scattered-access markers, device stores, and latency; use sufficient precision for Q and bias before addition
constraints: Validate layout and numerical changes separately
Prior-candidate captures cannot stand in for new-candidate measurements

records.signal: Repeated reference results disagree or traces show CPU fallback
records.mechanism: Reference paths, precision ordering, and runtime conditions affect comparability
records.action: Fix inputs, inspect allowed reference intervals, actual leaf operators/task paths, and report determinism conditions separately
constraints: Do not silently change global determinism or original tolerances
Slow CPU fallback does not establish the device optimization ceiling
Mixed CANN paths support reference analysis only and cannot enter Triton candidates
